title: First Amendment
summary: Added grounds for restricting free speech — public order, friendly relations with foreign states, incitement to offence. Also validated zamindari abolition laws.

title: Seventh Amendment
summary: Reorganised states on linguistic basis following States Reorganisation Act. Abolished Part B states.

title: Twenty-Fourth Amendment
summary: Restored Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution including Fundamental Rights, following Golak Nath case.

title: Twenty-Fifth Amendment
summary: Restricted right to property — allowed acquisition of property for public purposes without full market compensation.

title: Forty-Second Amendment
summary: Called the 'Mini Constitution' — added 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble, strengthened Centre vis-à-vis states, extended term of Lok Sabha and State Assemblies to 6 years during Emergency. Many provisions later struck down or amended.

title: Forty-Fourth Amendment
summary: Reversed many Emergency-era changes. Restored 5-year Lok Sabha term. Right to property removed from Fundamental Rights, made a legal right under Article 300A.

title: Fifty-Second Amendment (Anti-Defection Law)
summary: Added the Tenth Schedule — disqualifies MPs and MLAs who defect from their party or vote against party line without permission. Foundation of the anti-defection framework.

title: Sixty-First Amendment
summary: Lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years for Lok Sabha and state assembly elections.

title: Seventy-Third Amendment (Panchayati Raj)
summary: Gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions. Added Part IX and Eleventh Schedule. Mandated elections, reservations for women and SCs/STs in panchayats.

title: Seventy-Fourth Amendment (Municipalities)
summary: Gave constitutional status to urban local bodies. Added Part IXA and Twelfth Schedule covering 18 functions for municipalities.

title: Eighty-Sixth Amendment (Right to Education)
summary: Made free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6–14 years under Article 21A. Basis for the Right to Education Act 2009.

title: Ninety-Seventh Amendment (Co-operative Societies)
summary: Gave constitutional status to co-operative societies — added Right to form co-operative societies as a Fundamental Right, added Part IXB.

title: Ninety-Ninth Amendment (NJAC)
summary: Replaced the collegium system for judicial appointments with a National Judicial Appointments Commission. Struck down by Supreme Court in 2015 as unconstitutional.

title: Hundredth Amendment (Land Boundary Agreement)
summary: Gave effect to the Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh — transferred enclaves to Bangladesh and received Bangladeshi enclaves.

title: Hundred-and-First Amendment (GST)
summary: Introduced the Goods and Services Tax — the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence. Added Articles 246A, 269A, 279A. Constituted the GST Council.

title: Hundred-and-Second Amendment (OBC Commission)
summary: Gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes.

title: Hundred-and-Third Amendment (EWS Reservation)
summary: Provided 10% reservation in government jobs and educational institutions for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among the general category. Upheld by Supreme Court in 2022.

title: Hundred-and-Fourth Amendment
summary: Extended reservation for SC/ST in Lok Sabha and state assemblies for another 10 years (to 2030). Removed reservation for Anglo-Indians.

title: Hundred-and-Sixth Amendment (Women's Reservation)
summary: Reserved one-third of seats in Lok Sabha and state assemblies for women. Reservation will only come into effect after the next delimitation exercise — now linked to the 131st Amendment process.

title: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026
summary: Proposes to increase Lok Sabha to 850 seats, restore population-proportional delimitation, and allow Parliament to decide by simple majority which census to use. Triggers implementation of 106th Amendment women's reservation. Currently pending in Lok Sabha — introduced April 16, 2026.
